audit_scope.description: This batch predominantly covers EL logic: EVM gas repricing (EIP-1884), precompile execution (EIP-198), difficulty adjustment (EIP-100), P2P networking protocols (EIP-8094, EIP-7975, EIP-7642), JSON-RPC interfaces (EIP-234, EIP-1193), DID authentication (EIP-2844), and EOF metadata (EIP-7834). All are EL-centric specifications.

in_scope: P2P Networking (devp2p eth/69, eth/70, blob distribution)

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via expensive opcodes/precompiles, log filter abuse, replay attacks on DID auth
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, false blob data, false block range claims, receipt manipulation
Gas exhaustion via MODEXP underpricing, exploiting gas repricing breakage in existing contracts

cl_vectors.threat: Not directly applicable to this batch but timestamp manipulation affects difficulty (EIP-100)

misclassified_entities.reason: In EIP-1193, the Wallet/Client is modeled as external but it is the trusted internal component that the Provider bridges to. However, from the Provider's perspective it is a separate program, so the classification is borderline acceptable. Retained as external since Provider and Wallet are explicitly stated to be separate programs.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON-RPC API (eth_getLogs, eth_newFilter with blockHash parameter)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public RPC endpoint, no authentication required. Any user can submit filter requests. Derived from EIP-234 EXT-RPC-CLIENT.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via EIP-1193 Provider
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Untrusted web application invoking Provider methods. DApps run in browser context and may be malicious. Derived from EIP-1193 EXT-DAPP and EXT-MALICIOUS-DAPP.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via DID Authentication RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External DApp requesting DID operations. Untrusted, may attempt replay attacks or request unauthorized path permissions. Derived from EIP-2844 EXT-DAPP-CLIENT.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: devp2p protocol (eth/69 handshake, eth/70 GetReceipts, GetPooledBlobs/PooledBlobs, BlockRangeUpdate, Transactions)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P network peer. May send invalid blob data, false block range claims, manipulated receipts, or malformed transactions. Derived from EIP-8094, EIP-7975, EIP-7642 peer entities.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Miner/Validator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header fields (timestamp, difficulty, uncle references)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers set timestamps and include uncle references that feed into difficulty calculation. May attempt to manipulate difficulty for issuance gaming. Derived from EIP-100 EXT-BLOCK-PROPOSER and EXT-ATTACKER-MINER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract/EOA via EVM CALL
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL to precompile address 0x05 (MODEXP) or contracts affected by gas repricing
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can invoke precompiles or trigger gas-sensitive code paths. May craft inputs to exploit gas mispricing. Derived from EIP-198 EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT and EIP-1884 EXT-CALLER.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployment Source (Compiler/Tool)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EOF container bytecode submitted for on-chain deployment
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Deployment source submits EOF bytecode with optional metadata. Metadata content is arbitrary and unvalidated at protocol level. Derived from EIP-7834 EXT-DEPLOYMENT-SOURCE.

trusted_external_entities.name: Verification Tool (Block Explorer)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Off-chain source verification using on-chain EOF metadata
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Verification tools consume metadata from deployed contracts. Metadata may be intentionally misleading. Derived from EIP-7834 EXT-VERIFICATION-TOOL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet/Client Software
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The Wallet is a separate program from the Provider but is assumed trusted. Semi-trusted because it is a distinct program that could theoretically be compromised, though EIP-1193 assumes it is secure. Derived from EIP-1193 EXT-WALLET.

trusted_external_entities.name: Ethereum Network (Remote RPC/Chain)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum network connectivity status feeds into Provider state machine. Network events are not authenticated. Derived from EIP-1193 EXT-ETHEREUM-NETWORK.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User (Human)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Human user who controls account permissions. Semi-trusted as the user is the authority for their own accounts but may make mistakes (social engineering). Derived from EIP-1193 EXT-USER.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Must validate mutual exclusivity of blockHash vs fromBlock/toBlock. Must validate blockHash format (32-byte hex). Must handle block-not-found gracefully. Rate limiting recommended to prevent DoS via expensive lookups.
Must validate RequestArguments structure. Must sanitize all input data. Must enforce rate limiting. Provider must not expose private data. Provider and Wallet must remain isolated programs.
All DApp requests are potentially malicious. Input sanitization, rate limiting, and Provider-Wallet isolation must be enforced. No private user data should be accessible from Provider.

Nonce must be validated for freshness to prevent replay attacks. Path permissions must be enforced for auto-decryption. User consent required for unmatched paths. JWS signatures must use proper cryptographic algorithms.
Must validate blob hash correspondence to vhashes. Must not forward transactions until all blobs are received and validated. Must handle missing/partial blob responses gracefully.

Must validate receipt count matches transaction count. Individual receipt size must be bounded by gas_limit/8. Total size must be bounded by block gas limit. Must handle pagination correctly and penalize peers sending invalid data.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: devp2p eth/69 Status handshake and BlockRangeUpdate (EIP-7642)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Must validate networkid, genesis hash, and forkid compatibility. Must verify peers actually serve claimed block ranges. Peers claiming false ranges should be penalized. BlockRangeUpdate rate should be bounded.

Timestamps must be bounded to prevent difficulty manipulation. Uncle references must be cryptographically verifiable via unclesHash. Difficulty adjustment formula must prevent issuance gaming through uncle rate manipulation.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: CALL to MODEXP precompile at address 0x05 (EIP-198)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Gas pricing must accurately reflect computational cost. Input lengths parsed from call data must be handled safely (zero-padding for short inputs, ignoring excess). Modulus-zero edge case must return zero. mult_complexity formula must not underestimate actual computation time.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EVM opcode execution (SLOAD, BALANCE, EXTCODEHASH) with EIP-1884 repricing
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Gas costs must reflect actual trie access cost. Contracts with hardcoded gas assumptions (2300 stipend for transfer/send, ERC-165 callbacks) may break. No protocol-level mitigation exists for existing contracts.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EOF container deployment with metadata section (EIP-7834)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Metadata section must be structurally validated (size range 1-65535, positioned before data section). Metadata content is opaque and unvalidated at protocol level. Metadata must not be reachable by contract code execution.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: On-chain EOF metadata consumption for source verification (EIP-7834)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Metadata content may be intentionally misleading. Verification tools must independently verify source by recompilation, not trust metadata claims. IPFS content availability is not guaranteed.
Wallet is assumed secure but is a separate program. Communication channel integrity must be maintained. Wallet responses (results, errors) must conform to ProviderRpcError specification.
Network connectivity events are not authenticated. Provider must correctly track connected/disconnected state. Chain ID changes must be properly propagated via events.

User decisions are authoritative for their accounts. Wallet must faithfully represent permissions. Revocations must be immediate and complete. Social engineering risks exist but are outside protocol scope.
